core_obligations: Treat the characteristic zero case: use the primitive element theorem to produce a separating transcendence basis and verify the Jacobian criterion after inverting one element (proof lines 9894-9920).
Treat the characteristic p case: use the existence of a p-basis and the same criterion (proof lines 9920-9945).
Combine the two cases to conclude the theorem (proof lines 9945-9951).
proof_roadmap: Split according to the characteristic of the base field (proof lines 9894-9900).
Characteristic zero: separating transcendence basis and the Jacobian criterion (proof lines 9900-9920).
Characteristic p: p-basis and the same criterion (proof lines 9920-9951).
difficulty_reason: The theorem proves that a finite type algebra over a field whose local rings are regular becomes formally smooth after inverting a single element, and the proof is a 58-line argument split according to the characteristic. In characteristic zero it uses the existence of a separating transcendence basis given by the primitive element theorem, and in characteristic p it uses the p-basis theory of the same chapter, together with the Jacobian criterion for formal smoothness. The two cases are treated separately and each is carried out with the explicit element that is to be inverted.
